text:
maria: quick check — ran a consumer-chat pilot comparing 13b-int8 vs 13b-int6 across ~10k requests. Preliminary notes: int8 looks ~35% cheaper but we see a nontrivial bump in hallucination rate and worse p99 latency. anyone seen similar?

aj: can you share the unit-econ calc + the exact quality signal you used?

maria: sure, pasted the quick calc below:
```
cost assumptions:
13b-int6 (quant profile A) = $0.95 / 1M tokens
13b-int8 = $0.58 / 1M tokens
avg tokens / request = 45
sample traffic ~20 rps sustained -> ~1.7M tokens/day
so int8 delta ~= $0.37/1M tokens -> ~ $630/day savings at that load
```

sam: nice. what's the quality measurement? which eval set?

maria: GTN longform QA slice (200 prompts). metrics: exact-match, F1, and manual false-assertion tag. results: int6 halluc rate 2.1% -> int8 3.9% (+1.8pp). EM dropped ~2.4 pts on extractive prompts.

linh: interesting — latency profiles too? int8 median seems lower but tail higher?

maria: yes — median int8 120ms vs int6 150ms; p99 int8 650ms vs int6 480ms. looks like more occasional tail stalls on int8.

prod_josh: from product POV our interactive chat p99 target is <500ms. int8 p99 650ms breaks that. But cost savings are meaningful for non-interactive flows.

maria: my tentative recommendation: do NOT push int8 as default for interactive chat. Consider enabling int8 for background/batch tasks (summaries, embeddings) where p99 and hallucination tolerance are higher. For chat, run a hybrid routing experiment: latency-sensitive traffic -> int6; best-effort/batch -> int8.

sam: I agree. propose we canary int8 at 5% traffic with two controls: quality gating (false-assertion delta) and latency gating (p99). Rollback if hallucination increases >0.5pp or p99 exceeds 520ms for the canary slice.

aj: operational checklist: need a model-variant pin, routing flag to split by session type, and autoscale pool adjustment (int8 pool can be smaller but need warmup policy). I'll sketch flags and pools.

eval-bot: smoke check summary: sample-level analysis shows hallucination bump concentrated on multi-step reasoning prompts and longer-context extracts. Short factual Qs look stable.

linh: that aligns with cache behavior — int8 kernel path seems to incur more KV cache churn in our runtime on longer sequences. We should try a warm-start KV cache for canary hosts. Also test a slightly increased kv-cache TTL for int8.

prod_josh: decisions for GTN / product: if canary passes (<=0.5pp halluc delta and p99 <=520ms) we can consider rolling to 20% with further monitoring. If not, we keep int6 for chat and document cost tradeoffs to GTN (savings per million tokens, expected monthly savings at X usage).

maria: next actionable steps (proposed):
1) @aj runs 5% canary for 48h (50k requests) with per-slice tagging (reasoning vs factual)
2) @linh applies warm-start KV tweak and increases TTL for int8 canary hosts
3) @sam runs priming A/B (small prompt-template tweaks) to see if int8 hallucination sensitivity reduces
4) @maria will produce a concise unit-econ + risk summary for GTN (one-pager)

aj: I'll own the canary + routing flag. filing infra ticket INFRA-2321 and will link the canary dashboard.

sam: also add a prompt-level fallback: if confidence score < threshold, route to int6 for a re-eval. easy to test in canary.

linh: small note — monitor GPU kernel OOMs/slowdowns; int8 kernel sometimes spikes on memory-bound sequences.

prod_josh: thanks — sync decision review on Thu EOD. please post results in this thread. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks team — I'll post the one-pager and the canary dashboard link once ready.
